:::{#thm-ols-resid-orthogonal}
#### Residuals are orthogonal to the covariates

Fit a linear regression model by maximum likelihood,
with design matrix $\mX$ of full column rank,
coefficient estimate $\evb$,
fitted values $\hat{\vy} \eqdef \mX\evb$,
and residual vector $\vresid \eqdef \vy - \hat{\vy}$.
Then:

$$
\underbrace{\tp{\mX}}_{(p+1) \times n} \underbrace{\vresid}_{n \times 1} = \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
$$ {#eq-ols-resid-orthogonal}

In particular,
if the model has an intercept,
the residuals add up to zero, $\sumin \resid_i = 0$,
and the residuals are orthogonal to the fitted values, $\sumin \hat y_i \resid_i = 0$.
:::
